varieties.name: Anne
varieties.summary: Fall-bearing golden raspberry with mild, sweet apricot-like flavor.
varieties.description: A fall-bearing (primocane) golden raspberry from a cooperative breeding program led by the University of Maryland with Rutgers, Virginia Tech and the University of Wisconsin–River Falls; patented 1998. Large conical berries with a mild, sweet flavor carrying apricot and banana notes and less tartness than red types.

varieties.name: Double Gold
varieties.summary: Cornell everbearing gold raspberry; champagne-to-peach colored fruit, two crops a year.
varieties.description: Released by Cornell University (Courtney Weber) in 2012. An everbearing raspberry giving summer and fall crops of golden-champagne to peachy-coral berries with mild, honey-like sweetness and low acidity.

varieties.name: Fall Gold
varieties.summary: Older everbearing golden raspberry; firm, sweet berries in summer and fall.
varieties.description: An older everbearing golden raspberry that can crop in both summer and fall, with big, firm, sweet golden berries. Widely sold; breeding history not captured here yet.

varieties.name: Cascade Gold
varieties.summary: Golden raspberry from the Pacific Northwest 'Cascade' series.
varieties.description: A golden raspberry in the Pacific Northwest 'Cascade' line. Limited detail gathered so far; watched because it's rarely offered.

varieties.name: Honey Queen
varieties.summary: Honey-colored raspberry sold by One Green World; limited public detail.
varieties.description: A honey-colored (red-gold) raspberry offered by One Green World. Limited independent documentation gathered so far.

varieties.name: Bristol
varieties.summary: Classic 1934 black raspberry; early, glossy, firm fruit with rich blackcap flavor.
varieties.description: A black raspberry from the New York State Agricultural Experiment Station at Geneva (Cornell), introduced 1934. Early-ripening, glossy, firm fruit with a rich, classic blackcap flavor that holds up well frozen; long one of the most widely grown black raspberries.

varieties.name: Jewel
varieties.summary: Cornell black raspberry; the most widely planted blackcap, good anthracnose resistance.
varieties.description: A Cornell-bred black raspberry (1970s). Large, firm, glossy fruit with rich, intensely sweet flavor and a hint of tartness; summer-bearing with strong anthracnose resistance. The most widely planted black raspberry commercially.

varieties.name: Niwot
varieties.summary: Primocane-fruiting black raspberry: two harvests a season.
varieties.description: A black raspberry patented by grower Peter Tallman, notable as a primocane-fruiting blackcap that gives two harvests a season (summer and fall) instead of fruiting only on second-year canes. Large, shiny fruit with a milder raspberry flavor; zones 4–8.

varieties.name: Ohio's Treasure
varieties.summary: Everbearing black raspberry; two crops a year, mid-August to mid-October.
varieties.description: A patented everbearing black raspberry (inventor Benjamin Dale Stokes) that crops on first-year canes from mid-August into October, with a possible early summer crop on overwintered canes. Large firm black fruit; zones 3–8.

varieties.name: Mac Black
varieties.summary: Late-season black raspberry used to extend the blackcap harvest.
varieties.description: A late-ripening black raspberry recommended by Nourse Farms for extending the season in U-pick and fresh-market plantings. Breeding history not captured here yet.

varieties.name: Munger
varieties.summary: Old black raspberry cultivar long grown in the Pacific Northwest.
varieties.description: An older black raspberry cultivar long grown commercially in the Pacific Northwest. Offered by One Green World; limited detail gathered so far.

varieties.name: Cumberland
varieties.summary: Heirloom black raspberry; sweet, firm, reliable.
varieties.description: An heirloom black raspberry grown for well over a century, valued for sweet, firm berries and reliability. Offered bare root by Food Forest Nursery.

varieties.name: Black Delicious
varieties.summary: Black raspberry listed by Hartmann's; limited public detail.
varieties.description: A black raspberry offered by Hartmann's Plant Company, so far only as a wholesale listing. Limited independent documentation.

varieties.name: Pequot Lakes
varieties.summary: Black raspberry listed by Hartmann's; limited public detail.
varieties.description: A black raspberry offered by Hartmann's Plant Company, currently out of stock. Limited independent documentation.

varieties.name: Shekinah 'Tahi'
varieties.summary: Marketed as the first fully spineless black raspberry.
varieties.description: Marketed by Raintree Nursery and Nourse Farms as the first completely spineless black raspberry. Genuinely unusual breeding rather than a rebrand; breeder not documented in what's been gathered so far.

varieties.name: Glencoe
varieties.summary: Thornless purple raspberry (red × black); cold-hardy, large firm berries.
varieties.description: A purple raspberry (red × black hybrid) notable for being thornless. Cold-hardy with large, firm berries good fresh or for jam.

varieties.name: Royalty
varieties.summary: Cornell purple raspberry (1982); very high yields, aphid resistant.
varieties.description: A purple raspberry released by Cornell's New York State Agricultural Experiment Station (1982). Large purple fruit with black-raspberry undertones at full ripeness, very high yields and outstanding aphid resistance; excellent for jams.

varieties.name: Brandywine
varieties.summary: Cornell purple raspberry; tart, intensely flavored, prized for jam.
varieties.description: A purple raspberry from Cornell's Geneva program. Large, intensely flavored reddish-purple fruit that turns bright red when cooked; a classic for jam, jelly and wine. Vigorous 5–6 ft canes need trellising.

varieties.name: Purple Dream
varieties.summary: Purple raspberry listed by Hartmann's; limited public detail.
varieties.description: A purple raspberry offered by Hartmann's Plant Company, currently out of stock. Limited independent documentation.

varieties.name: Crimson Night
varieties.summary: Cornell dark-foliage raspberry; deep red fruit on dark purple canes.
varieties.description: Released by Cornell University (Courtney Weber) in 2012 alongside Double Gold. An everbearing red raspberry grown as much for its dark crimson fruit and dark purple canes and foliage as for the harvest.

varieties.name: English Thornless
varieties.summary: Thornless red raspberry; easy picking.
varieties.description: A thornless red raspberry offered by Edible Landscaping. Included for its thornless canes rather than its color.

varieties.name: Canby Thornless
varieties.summary: Nearly thornless summer red raspberry from the Pacific Northwest.
varieties.description: A nearly thornless summer-bearing red raspberry. Included for its thornless canes rather than its color.

varieties.name: Polka
varieties.summary: Polish-bred primocane raspberry, notable for very early fall ripening.
varieties.description: A Polish-bred primocane (fall-bearing) raspberry, carried over from the original log for its very early fall ripening.

varieties.name: Emerald Carpet
varieties.summary: Creeping, ground-cover raspberry relative with small edible fruit.
varieties.description: A low, creeping ground-cover bramble with small edible fruit, grown as an evergreen carpet. A novelty rather than a production berry.

varieties.name: Black Hawk
varieties.summary: Vigorous, heat- and drought-tolerant black raspberry with big, firm berries.
varieties.description: A black raspberry noted for vigorous, extra-hardy plants that keep producing in hot, dry weather. Big, juicy, sweet, firm black berries that ripen in mid-July in zone 6; breeding history not documented in sources gathered so far.

varieties.name: Allen
varieties.summary: Black raspberry bred from Bristol x Cumberland; large glossy aromatic fruit.
varieties.description: A black raspberry bred from a Bristol x Cumberland cross, combining Bristol's fruit quality and cold hardiness with Cumberland's productivity. Large, firm, glossy black berries with rich aromatic sweetness, ripening in July on vigorous 4-5 ft plants.

varieties.name: Born Free
varieties.summary: Thornless black raspberry with deep purple, self-fertile fruit.
varieties.description: A thornless black raspberry sold by Gurney's Seed & Nursery, forming vase-shaped 4-7 ft canes with deep purple fruit ripening mid-June to mid-July. Self-fertile and reported free of significant pest or disease issues; breeder not documented in sources gathered so far.
